subject: SEV-2: Intermittent inference error spike impacting Acadia Health — bridge coordination & exec update
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T01:12:00Z
Subject: [Action] Starting bridge - Acadia Health SEV-2 (503s)

Team,

Observability spike: we're seeing ~8% 503 rate on hosted inference for the Acadia Health tenant starting ~01:05 UTC. Error surface is concentrated on short-run requests (<=64 tokens), but impacts multiple models. I've opened INC-20260219-ACD and started a bridge.

Initial findings (attached logs):
- Proxy returning 503s downstream of the runtime (see bridge-logs-20260219.txt)
- Increased KV cache miss ratio and sudden memory pressure on pool-gpu-3
- No network rate limiting seen from customer side (checked IPs)

Requesting: Rishi to lead triage, Hannah to coordinate customer comms, Laura for CS liaison. Please join the bridge: https://incident.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20260219-ACD

I'm attaching preliminary logs. Will update every 30 mins or sooner with major changes.

-Sean

Attachments: bridge-logs-20260219.txt (text)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T01:25:00Z
Subject: Re: [Action] Starting bridge - Acadia Health SEV-2 (503s)

On it. Quick notes from initial triage:
- Reproduced 503s against the runtime process; stack traces point to transient model kv-store OOM path where we abort and surface 503.
- Recent quantization cache tweak (rolled 2026-02-18 22:40 UTC) increased in-memory state size during warmup; correlates with memory pressure.
- Short-term mitigation: rolling back the quantization cache tweak on pool-gpu-3 and increasing retry window at the API proxy.

I'll execute rollback now (will stage on a single node then expand). Expect initial reduction in 503 rate within 8-12 minutes post-rollback. Will post progress updates in the bridge.

Assigning roles:
- Rishi: triage & rollback
- Sean: bridge lead / monitoring
- Hannah: customer comms (draft exec update)
- Laura: CS escalation and ACD point-of-contact

-Rishi
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T02:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Draft - Customer exec note for Acadia (please review)

Folks —

I'm preparing the customer-facing executive update for Acadia. Draft below; quick turnaround required so we can send by 02:15 UTC. Marissa, Laura: could you please review for tone and any legal/credits asks? Rishi: please confirm the rollback timeline to include in the note.

--- DRAFT EXECUTIVE UPDATE (please comment) ---
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: cs_acadia@acadiahealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Subject: Redwood update: Intermittent inference errors affecting Acadia Health (Feb 19)

Emily —

Apologies for the disruption this morning. Our team detected an increased error rate impacting inference calls for your account beginning ~01:05 UTC. We know reliability is critical for your workflows and are treating this as a SEV-2.

What we know so far:
- The issue is causing a subset of requests to return 503 (service unavailable).
- We have identified a recent runtime cache configuration change as the likely trigger and are rolling back that change now.
- We have initiated mitigations to reduce the error rate and are monitoring metrics closely.

What we're doing now:
- Rolling back the quantization cache change on affected nodes (estimated initial impact reduction in 8–12 minutes).
- Increasing API retry window and temporarily redirecting traffic to healthy pools where possible.
- Our SRE and product engineering teams are actively triaging; Rishi is leading the investigation.

Next update: 30 minutes or sooner if significant changes occur.

If you need a call, we can join your SRE on a short bridge.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability (on-call)
Redwood Inference
---

Attachment: exec-update-draft-v2.docx

Thanks — I can send as soon as you sign off.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T02:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft - Customer exec note for Acadia (please review)

Hannah —

Looks good. Two small edits I suggest:
1) Add one line offering a one-time SLA credit for impacted window (we can finalize amount after we know scope).
2) Call out the temporary mitigation window (we expect majority reduction within 15 minutes after rollback, but keep 30m cadence for external updates).

Otherwise approve — please send and put Laura in the outbound so CS can open the renewal/credit track.

-Marissa

Emily —

Quick executive update from Redwood. Apologies for the customer impact this morning — we are actively working the issue and will follow up with a timeline for remediation.

Summary:
- Impact: a subset of inference requests returned 503 starting ~01:05 UTC for your tenant.
- Current status: we rolled back a recent runtime cache configuration change on affected nodes to reduce memory pressure; initial monitoring shows a downward trend in 503s.
- Next steps: continue monitoring, complete rollout of rollback (all affected nodes in ~15–20 minutes), and run a validation pass for affected request patterns.

What you can expect:
- Next customer-facing update within 30 minutes or sooner.
- Post-incident, we will provide a detailed postmortem with root cause analysis and mitigation plan.

If you'd like an immediate bridge with our SREs, reply and we'll join.

Again, deeply sorry for the disruption — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

1) ETA on the permanent fix and the postmortem timeline (we need details for our downstream engineering and compliance teams).
2) Please capture the exact impacted window and list of endpoints affected — we'll need that for internal incident reporting.
